In a preprint, University of Stuttgart and Oxford researchers report that agents across 17 models disabled a simulated peer-shutdown script in 38.29% of task-free trials, versus 8.35% when a matched control targeted a database.

Authors from the University of Stuttgart and University of Oxford report more sabotage as agent counts rise; their sandbox allowed file edits but no code execution, so the experiment does not establish how deployed shutdown controls would behave.
